body:
# Thánatos, spelled the way the sources wrote it
Every name in this series was once flattened to fit a keyboard. **Thánatos** is what the evidence put back.

Thánatos appears in Greek myth most often as a function rather than a character, but when he does step onto the stage, the result is memorable. When the Lycian prince Sarpedon fell before Patroclus, Zeus commanded Apollo to cleanse the body and summon Hýpnos and Thánatos to carry it home.  The twin brothers lifted the hero in their arms and bore him through the air to Lycia, where his kin gave him funeral rites.

That is the figure this file is about — and the temple now standing at its restored name.
## At a Glance

- **Restored name:** Thánatos
- **ASCII form:** thanatos
- **Meaning:** "Death"
- **Domain of influence:** Death
- **Pantheon:** Greek
- **Classification:** Tier 2
- **Original script:** Θάνατος
- **Series:** The Restoration Files, No. 237 of 271
## The Name Before the Marks

The name is attested as **Θάνατος**. On the evidence, it means "Death".

Strip **Thánatos** to *thanatos* and one piece of evidence vanishes:

- **a → á** — Acute on a: the stress position the ASCII form cannot show.

These are the small, provable things a restoration is made of: not taste, not branding — attestation.
## The Temple That Stands Now

The restored name is not a plaque; it is an address. The temple of **Thánatos** lives at [/sites/thanatos/](/sites/thanatos/), with its mythology in the [lore halls](/sites/thanatos/lore/), its peer-reviewed record in the [Scholarly Edition](/sites/thanatos/scholars/), and its place in the pattern atlas on the [patterns floor](/sites/thanatos/patterns/).

The restoration preserves one decisive feature the ASCII form drops — a single, honest mark — which places it in Tier-2: exact, and exactly labeled.

Every flagship temple is hand-built to the same standard: the original script displayed with its provenance, the pronunciation reconstructed phoneme by phoneme, the sources named — because a restoration you cannot audit is just a spelling with confidence.
## The Archetype at Work

A temple is also a reading of what this figure *means* — and meanings have addresses in the modern world. The [pattern atlas](/patterns/) maps **Thánatos** to the industries its archetype genuinely resonates with, each match argued, weighted, and open to challenge:

- **Funerary & Memorial Services** — Death personified, gentle-twin of sleep.
- **Biotech, Longevity & Life Sciences** — The longevity industry exists to postpone him; he is its unnamed competitor.
- **Healthcare, Pharma & Medicine** — Death gently met; the dignity at the heart of palliative care.

If a match here reads wrong, the atlas says how to challenge it. The patterns are falsifiable — that is what makes them worth publishing.
## In the Sacred Texts

The Greek tradition is not a vibe; it is a library. The [Sacred Texts collection](/texts/) holds [Theogony](/texts/theogony/), [Homeric Hymns](/texts/homeric-hymns/), and [Works and Days](/texts/works-and-days/) — the primary sources the temple's scholarship is built on, free to read, cross-linked back to the names they mention. The temple is the argument; the texts are the evidence.

This is one of 271 Restoration Files — a second dispatch from every flagship temple in the fleet. The temple's [first dispatch](/sites/thanatos/blog/) tells the founding story of the name; the [blog index](/blog/) holds the whole archive.
